articles.title: Researchers May Have Solved a Puzzling Contradiction in the Ryugu Sample
articles.summary: Asteroids are critically different than their planetary counterparts. (Courtesy: JAXA) There's obviously no soil on Ryugu, but there is aqueous alteration.
articles.summary_short: Asteroids are critically different than their planetary counterparts. (Courtesy: JAXA) There's obviously no soil on Ryugu, but there is aqueous alteration.
articles.summary_long:
The Solar System's asteroids are sometimes referred to as fossils because they preserve evidence of the conditions when the Solar System formed. Asteroids are critically different than their planetary counterparts. Aqueous alteration isn't a rare action that happens only in space environments; it's common on Earth.

(Courtesy: JAXA) There's obviously no soil on Ryugu, but there is aqueous alteration. There seems to be two components, each altered under a different set of aqueous conditions. An asteroid can be clumpy on a macroscale, but how can it have two components in the same mineral matrix?

They found the expected serpentine and saponite, but they also identified something else: poorly crystalline magnesium silicate hydrate (M-S-H). Much of their matrices could be poorly crystalline M-S-H. That sample should be on Earth five years from now.

articles.title: In 2013, Researchers Pulled Recognizable Faces of Bystanders Out of the Eye Reflections in a Portrait
articles.summary: The face was a reflection in another person's eye. A 102-megapixel file puts you about 3.5 times above it.
articles.summary_short: The face was a reflection in another person's eye. A 102-megapixel file puts you about 3.5 times above it.
articles.summary_long:
An anonymous peer reviewer worked through a manuscript, looked at one of its figures, and recognized one of the authors. The face was a reflection in another person's eye. The subject's face, hair excluded, took up about 12 million of them.

The iris took about 54,000, which the authors note is under 0.5% of frontal face area. Out of that iris, they cropped rectangles 27 to 36 pixels wide by 42 to 56 pixels high, framed head and shoulders like a tiny passport photo. Average face area inside those crops was 322 pixels.

At identical framing, a bystander crop that ran 27 to 36 pixels wide in 2013 comes out around 44 to 58 pixels wide today, and 322 pixels of face area becomes about 839. A 102-megapixel file puts you about 3.5 times above it. The GFX100 II's pixel pitch works out to 43.8 mm across 11,648 pixels, or 3.76 micrometers.

articles.title: Jeffrey Gibson’s ‘A Real Love Thing’ Surveys a Decade of the Artist’s Multidisciplinary Practice
articles.summary: Through abstract, prismatic acrylic paintings to garment-like sculptures and textile collages, Jeffrey Gibson explores questions of identity, lineage, and cultural translation. Working across media, the artist intricately beads monumental works and incorporates a wide range of fabrics and materials.

articles.summary_long:
Through abstract, prismatic acrylic paintings to garment-like sculptures and textile collages, Jeffrey Gibson explores questions of identity, lineage, and cultural translation. Working across media, the artist intricately beads monumental works and incorporates a wide range of fabrics and materials. Jeffrey Gibson: A Real Love Thing at Johns Hopkins University Bloomberg Center delves into the cross-disciplinary breadth of the artist’s practice throughout the past decade.

Drawing on the early and continuing influence of music, the artist often integrates song lyrics into tapestry-like wall hangings and three-dimensional works. Music also inspired the title of the exhibition, which Gibson drew from a 1971 interview with soul artist Marvin Gaye, who described his seminal album What’s Going On by saying, “I think I’ve got a real love thing going. I love people, I love life, and I love nature, and I can’t see why other people can’t be like that.” Reflecting this sentiment, Gibson’s approach is a luminous celebration of Indigenous symbolism and traditional materials, such as jingle cones used in ceremonial garments, tipi poles, and glass beads that have coated bags, moccasins, and other apparel hand-crafted by Native Americans throughout the centuries.

The artist also posits a future full of hope, joy, acceptance, and, like Gaye, a love-above-all ethos. A Real Love Thing continues through March 13 at the Bloomberg Center in Washington, D.C., where Gibson will present a talk as part of the esteemed Sam Gilliam Lecture series on November 12. And if you’re near Eugene, Oregon, the artist’s traveling solo exhibition They Teach Love is also on view through through March 7 at the University of Oregon.

L'enquête préliminaire évoque la compromission d'un ordinateur portable appartenant à un ingénieur DevOps. Face à l'ampleur de l'attaque, plusieurs acteurs majeurs de l'écosystème financier numérique ont rapidement réagi. Tether, Circle et Ripple ont notamment participé au gel d'une partie des actifs dérobés. En juin, la Région a mis fin à sa collaboration avec l’agence Berger & Berger , chargée de la rénovation, en invoquant une « défaillance ». Le projet a aussi été revu à la baisse : l’Institut occupera environ 2 600 m² , contre 3 900 m² prévus jusqu’ici. La Région parle d’un simple « contretemps ».

Gretchen Scherer ’s paintings of affluent homes, studios, and libraries appear to expand before our eyes. Brimming with ornately framed paintings installed salon-style on richly papered walls, her half-imagined spaces are inspired by real places, which she infuses with a playful brightness and whimsy. When we home in on one particular floral arrangement, framed artwork, or piece of furniture, it seems that there’s a sudden increase in how much more there is to explore.

Scherer’s new solo exhibition, In Time at Monya Rowe Gallery , continues the artist’s fascination with historical interiors, from art museums and drawing rooms to palatial halls and ecclesiastical spaces. The artist leans into a kind of escapism or longing for not only elegant, luminous surroundings but a desire to immerse oneself, quite literally, in the world of art. In our era of steel, glass, concrete, and contractor gray interiors, Scherer celebrates craftsmanship and beauty.

Fantastical convergences of art history and architecture occur in pieces like “A French Cafe with Paintings,” where a Beaux Arts interior transforms into an ad hoc gallery with myriad famous works casually strewn about. Working in oil, Scherer’s choice of media nods to the same used to create many of the historical examples she includes. In Time opens today and continues through January 9 in New York.

Face à l'afflux attendu de correctifs de failles découvertes par l'IA sur les logiciels open source, IBM et Red Hat présentent le projet Lightwell. Cette plateforme combinant IA et expertise humaine sert de couche de coordination pour intégrer les patchs dans la supply chain logicielle des entreprises sans interruption de service. Il revendiqué la découverte de plusieurs milliers de failles dans des applications open source.

Pour répondre à ces problématiques, IBM et sa filiale Red Hat viennent de présenter le projet Lightwell, doté d’un budget de 5 Md$ et mobilisant 20 000 ingénieurs des deux sociétés. L’objectif de l’initiative est de créer une plateforme pour accélérer la détection et la correction des vulnérabilités dans les logiciels open source. Aucune mise à niveau ni accès au code source n’est requis.

Les entreprises pourront partager des vulnérabilités sensibles sous embargo via un « modèle d'intermédiaire sécurisé » et recevoir des correctifs validés pour les plateformes Red Hat et le code de la communauté indépendante. Elles pourront également déployer des correctifs sur l'ensemble des chaînes de dépendances, signaler et résoudre les problèmes dans les environnements de production actifs, et partager les correctifs en amont afin que la communauté open source puisse les intégrer. « Nous voulons nous assurer que tous les correctifs que nous fournissons aux entreprises via la plateforme soient également mis à la disposition de la communauté open source qui a développé le code », explique Ashesh Badani, vice-président senior et directeur des produits chez Red Hat, à CSOonline .

Cela fait des années que la firme à la pomme travaille sur la protection cryptographique post-quantique. Cette protection sécurise à la fois les conversations et leurs clés de chiffrement contre de futures attaques quantiques.

L’entreprise pense qu’en le publiant de cette manière, les chercheurs en sécurité pourront vraiment mettre ces protections à l'épreuve pour s'assurer qu'elles fonctionneront lorsque l'informatique quantique deviendra véritablement une menace. articles.summary: A flaw in Telegram for Android could be chained with two other bugs to take full control of a victim's phone through a voice call, once the victim answered, according to security startup NebuSec. The attacker needed only an ordinary Telegram account.
